detail.title: Operational Criteria for Publicly Reliable Physical Records
detail.question: What are the necessary operational conditions for a quantum state to qualify as a stable, publicly accessible objective record?
detail.reason: Maintaining active investigation into the operational criteria for objective states and their environmental encoding.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Publicly Reliable Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective physical records are defined by the proliferation of pointer states into the environment, enabling multiple observers to access consistent information without disturbing the system. Redundancy, enforced via decoherence, is the necessary mechanism for this transition from quantum superposition to classical objectivity.
detail.reason: Revision of notebook nb-objective-records-01 to synthesize new theoretical findings regarding record accessibility and decoherence.

detail.title: Synthesis of Operational Criteria and Robustness in Objective Record Formation
detail.summary: This cycle advances the investigation into objective records by revising three core notebooks to incorporate recently processed evidence. We refine the operational definitions of physical records, clarify the relationship between scrambling dynamics and decoherence, and solidify the criteria for robust observer agreement, aligning all findings with available quantum Darwinism literature.
